posts.title: A compassion checklist for people building AI agents
posts.dek: Agents act, so their failures are actions as well as words. A practical checklist that maps the benchmark's compassion dimensions to concrete agent design decisions.

posts.title: How to read an AI model release for welfare and safety signals
posts.dek: A system card or release note can be read for specific, checkable disclosures. Here is what to look for, what is often missing, and what to ask.

posts.title: The case for compassion-first AI, with what we know and what we don't
posts.dek: The credible case rests on duty of care, regulation, liability and procurement. The commercial upside is plausible but unproven, and we say where the evidence runs out.

posts.title: What "compassion-first AI" means, and what it does not
posts.dek: Compassion-first AI is a set of observable behaviours for recognising, responding to and reducing suffering, not a warm tone, agreeableness or a refusal policy.

posts.title: Why AI labs should be assessed on organisational compassion, not only model behaviour
posts.dek: A model is one snapshot of what a lab ships; governance, incident response and disclosure are decided by the organisation, and they need their own measurement.

posts.title: Why we do not rank AI models yet, and what would change that
posts.dek: Declining to rank models is a methodological position with stated conditions, set by a public item bank, a single judge family and no human validation yet.
